Beyond the switch: what API's own data, the 2027 calendar and the recertification rules add

The sections above cover what changed in September 2024 and how to plan a test-centre sitting. This section covers what most planning guides leave out. It draws on API's own published statistics on remote testing and pass rates, the 2027 core-exam calendar, the state of the remote-eligible list in late 2026, the online recertification quiz and its one trap, the move to digital certificates, and what the change means for Canadian inspectors heading for a provincial credential. Every figure comes from an API Individual Certification Programs (ICP) publication or another regulator's public document, with the date of that document. We avoid secondhand numbers. Fees are left to API's Schedules and Fees page because they change.

How big remote testing became before API withdrew it for the core five

Remote testing was not a small side channel. That is why its withdrawal still causes questions two years later. API's ICP status reports give the history. Remote exams were piloted with the specialised computer-based programmes in November 2020 and opened to all programmes in February 2021. The status report dated 30 October 2023 says API had given more than 5,000 remote exams since 2020, including more than 1,800 in 2023 up to the end of October. API's status report dated April 2024 puts the running total above 7,000.

The same October 2023 report breaks remote volume down by programme for 2020 to October 2023. The core inspector exams led: 1,292 remote API 510 exams, 1,167 for API 570, 906 for API 1169 and 599 for API 653. API 580 was the largest of the programmes that stayed remote, with 795. So the programmes that lost remote delivery were the ones used most remotely. Teams that had come to rely on remote 510 and 570 sittings for people on rotation felt the change most.

The report as of 30 April 2025 records the decision in one line: the remote modality "was suspended for the core programs (API 510, 570, 653, 1169 and 1184) in September 2024 and is currently only offered for specialized and smaller programs." API's exam scheduling page says the same thing today. If an older guide, a recruiter or a forum post tells your candidate they can sit API 510 from home, it predates September 2024.

The statistics also show where the candidates are. Between 2015 and April 2024, the United States accounted for 54,569 API exams and Canada for 10,805, the two largest totals of any country, according to the April 2025 report. For North American employers that is reassuring. Prometric's network is densest where most API candidates already live, and API says its computer-based exams can be taken at more than 500 Prometric locations.

Did test-centre-only delivery change pass rates? API's published numbers

This is the question behind a lot of the rumour traffic: did moving the core exams back into test centres make them harder to pass? API publishes per-window results in its ICP status update reports, so you can look rather than guess. The table below is taken from the report dated 30 April 2025. September 2024 was the first test-centre-only API 510 window, October 2024 the first for API 570, and November 2024 the first for API 653.

ProgrammeLast three windows with remote availableFirst windows test-centre only
API 510September 2023: 64.0%; January 2024: 69.2%; May 2024: 68.5%September 2024: 65.9%; January 2025: 66.9%
API 570October 2023: 67.3%; February 2024: 66.0%; June 2024: 68.4%October 2024: 70.2%; February 2025: 63.7%
API 653November 2023: 71.5%; March 2024: 69.0%; July 2024: 75.9%November 2024: 64.9%; March 2025: 62.9%

Read these with three cautions. First, API reports them per window for all candidates, so first attempts and retakes are mixed together. A window with many retakers can look quite different from one dominated by first-timers. Second, two or three windows are too few to show cause and effect. API 653's two test-centre-only windows were lower than the window before, but API 570's first test-centre-only window was the highest of the six shown. Third, candidate numbers move as well. API 510 had 1,211 candidates in September 2024 and 997 in January 2025.

What the published data does support is narrower and more useful. Pass rates for the core codes stayed broadly in the same range after the change, and in every window roughly a third of candidates did not pass. For a planner that means the delivery mode is not what decides the result. Eligibility, preparation time and choosing the right window decide it. Plan on the assumption that some candidates will need a second window. Under API's rules that is a new application for a later window, not a same-window retest.

The remote-eligible list in late 2026: TES sunset, API 982 added

API's August 2024 notice listed the programmes that kept both remote and in-person delivery: API TES, 982, 571, 577, 580, 936, SIFE, SIRE, SIEE, AQ1 and AQ2. Two later developments change how that list reads today.

  • API TES (Tank Entry Supervisor) has been sunset. API sunset the TES programme in December 2025, so it no longer appears among bookable exams even though the 2024 notice still lists it.
  • API 982 (refractory inspector) is new. The April 2025 status report says API 982 was introduced in August 2024. It sits on the remote-eligible list alongside API 936.

For a mechanical-integrity team the practical list is simple. API 571, 577 and 580 are the add-on credentials inspectors most often pursue after a core code, and all three can still be taken remotely. That makes the second credential much easier to fit around a rotation than the first. The ultrasonic examiner qualifications (the QUTE family) were never remote. API delivers them as performance demonstrations in five-day sessions. The April 2025 report also notes that the QUTE programmes were consolidated in 2025 into QUTE (M) and QUTE (PA).

2027 core exam windows and application deadlines

Because a scheduled exam cannot be moved to another window, the calendar matters more than the proctoring mode. API has published its 2027 windows. The table lists the core programmes with the application deadlines shown on API's Schedules and Fees page. Confirm the deadline on api.org before you commit a candidate, because API can adjust dates.

Two planning points follow. The January 2027 API 510 deadline falls on 29 October 2026, so a supervisor deciding in late autumn whether to put someone forward has very little time. And in 2027 the API 570 window starts at the end of January, closer to the API 510 window than in 2026. A candidate who wants both credentials early in the year can apply for both, but should be honest about whether they can prepare for two calculation-heavy exams a month apart. For the 2026 calendar and how to book, see the API 510, 570 and 653 exam schedule.

The exam material changes as well. The API 510 publications effectivity sheet covering the September 2026, January 2027 and May 2027 exams lists newer editions of several referenced documents, including the 2025 ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and the 5th edition of API RP 576. Candidates studying from an older code set should download the current effectivity sheet from the API 510 programme page before buying books. API sets what is examinable, and it moves with each cycle.

The recertification quiz is online, but it has a trap that leads back to a test centre

For inspectors who are already certified, the end of remote testing changes less than people fear. API 510, 570 and 653 recertification every three years is based on documented inspection activity (at least 20 percent of time over the cycle), 24 hours of continuing professional development (CPD), and an online open-book quiz every six years, according to the programme pages. No test-centre visit is involved.

There is a catch, and API's API 570 programme page states it directly: failing the web quiz twice means retaking the full exam. Since September 2024 that full exam is only available at a Prometric centre. An inspector who treats the six-year quiz casually can therefore end up back in a test-centre window, on the same calendar and deadline rules as a new candidate. The quiz is 25 questions focused on code changes, with a four-hour limit. Prepare for it by reading what changed in the current editions, not by relying on memory of the edition you first sat.

Two CPD rules are also worth checking before the recertification date. API's inspector recertification programme document (revised September 2025) accepts only CPD evidence showing verifiable instructional contact time or CEUs, and API's CPD guidance does not accept activities related to maintaining an ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification. NDT technicians who also hold an API code certificate should therefore not assume their NDT refresher or recertification hours count toward API CPD. Check API's current programme document, and plan code-related CPD separately.

Digital certificates and verifying a crew's credentials

The other administrative change since 2024 is how certificates exist. API's Program Updates page records that starting in June 2025 ICP began publishing certifications in digital form, and that it was migrating more than 75,000 certifications to the digital platform. Combined with instant scoring, the result is that a candidate who passes at a test centre gets a Prometric score report within 24 hours, the result reaches the ICP portal within three business days, and the credential is digital. There is no longer a wait for a paper certificate before prequalification paperwork can move.

For owners and contractors that also changes verification. Instead of accepting a photocopied certificate in a bid package, check the credential against API's own records. API maintains a public inspector search for this. A certificate that cannot be found there, or whose dates do not match the bid package, is a question to resolve before the inspector signs anything. For how owners set these expectations in contracts, see our API inspector guide.

Canada: in Alberta the test-centre exam is only the first step

For Canadian inspectors the API exam often leads to a provincial credential. In Alberta, ABSA's AB-526 (In-Service Pressure Equipment Inspector Certification Requirements, Edition 3 Revision 3, issued 17 January 2025) sets the route. For the pressure vessels and pressure piping certificate, a candidate must hold an API 510 certificate or show they passed the API 510 exam within the previous five years. For the piping-only certificate, API 570 plays the same role, and a National Board in-service route also exists. ABSA then runs its own exam: 100 multiple-choice questions in three hours, with a 70 percent pass mark, using official hard-copy references only. AB-526 explains that the ABSA exam does not repeat the technical content of the API or National Board bodies of knowledge. It tests Alberta legislation and ABSA requirements.

So for an Alberta candidate the end of remote API testing adds a Prometric trip to a two-exam path. The five-year validity of the API exam result for ABSA purposes gives some slack, though. A candidate can pass API 510 in one year and sit the ABSA exam later, as long as it is within the five-year window. Other provinces have their own requirements. Confirm with the regulator where the equipment is located.

Where NDT certification fits for the same field crews

Most crews that include API inspectors also include the technicians who produce the thickness readings, scans and indications those inspectors evaluate. Their credential is different. NDT personnel are qualified and certified by their employer to a written practice under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or through ASNT's central programmes. That certification is not affected by any API delivery change, and API certification does not replace it. Under SNT-TC-1A, a Level II sets up and calibrates equipment, interprets and evaluates results against the applicable code or specification, and reports them, within one NDT method.

Atlantis NDT does not offer API 510, 570 or 653 training, exam preparation or proctoring. For those, apply to API ICP directly. What we offer is the complementary path. We provide ASNT SNT-TC-1A NDT training online, live-virtual or onsite (NDT Level II training, ASNT Level III, ASNT certification paths), and more than 1,000 technicians have been trained. We also perform NDE for in-service equipment, with results delivered to the owner's API-certified inspector, who remains the inspector of record (see API 510 NDE support). Ask for an ASNT NDT training plan for your crew. We reply with a quote within 24 hours.

Did pass rates drop after API moved 510, 570 and 653 back to test centres?

Not in a consistent way. API's report dated 30 April 2025 shows API 510 at 65.9 percent (September 2024) and 66.9 percent (January 2025), API 570 at 70.2 and 63.7 percent, and API 653 at 64.9 and 62.9 percent in their first test-centre-only windows. Those are all-candidate figures and too few windows to show cause and effect.

Is the TES exam still on the remote list?

API sunset the TES programme in December 2025, so it is no longer bookable even though API's 2024 notice listed it. API 982, introduced in August 2024, is on the remote-eligible list.

Can failing the recertification web quiz send me back to a Prometric centre?

Yes. API's API 570 programme page says failing the web quiz twice requires retaking the full exam, and the full core exams are test-centre only.

Do ASNT NDT training hours count toward API CPD?

Do not assume so. API's CPD guidance excludes activities related to maintaining ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification and, since September 2025, requires verifiable contact time or CEUs. Check API's current programme document.

When is the first API 510 window of 2027?

2 to 22 January 2027, with an application deadline of 29 October 2026, according to API's Schedules and Fees page. Confirm on api.org before applying.

Need NDE data for an API inspector while your crew works through its certifications? Request an inspection quote, or plan ASNT Level II training for your technicians.

Sources for this section: API ICP Status Update reports dated 30 October 2023 and 30 April 2025 (api.org); API ICP Program Updates (29 August 2024; June 2025 digital credential notices); API ICP Examinations and Schedules and Fees pages; API 510 and API 570 programme pages; ABSA AB-526 Edition 3 Revision 3 (absa.ca). Checked 4 October 2026.
